title: He was not there.
paragraphs: “He is not here, but is risen.” — Luke 24:6
The lesson I learned from the empty tomb is this: God’s greatest victory can look like unbearable loss before the morning comes.

Friday looked final.
The cross looked like defeat.
The sealed grave looked like silence.

While sorrow sat heavy on human hearts, God was already writing resurrection into the story. And that speaks to me deeply, because there are seasons when my prayers feel buried, my strength feels gone, and hope feels like a stone rolled over everything I love.
The tomb was empty, not because pain was fake, but because Jesus is greater than death.

The resurrection is not motivational poetry.
It is the crushing of the grave.
It is the public victory of Christ over sin, hell, shame, and the power of darkness.

And that means my worst moment does not get the final word.
My sin does not get the final word.
My failure does not get the final word.
Death does not get the final word.

The empty tomb teaches me that when God seems silent, He may be preparing a miracle too holy for my eyes to see yet. It teaches me that what looks over can become the very place where grace announces a new beginning. It teaches me that resurrection is not only something Christ experienced—it is the life He now gives to every sinner who repents and believes in Him.
Because let us be clear: the empty tomb is only good news if we know why He went there in the first place.

Jesus died for our sins.
He took our guilt.
He bore our judgment.
And He rose again so that whoever trusts in Him would not perish, but have everlasting life.

That is the Gospel.
Not self-help.
Not religion.
Rescue.
So the lesson I learned from the empty tomb is simple, but it burns in my soul:
Never call it dead when Jesus has promised life.

If your heart is tired, come to Christ.
If your past is filthy, come to Christ.
If your faith is weak, come to Christ.
The stone has been rolled away.
Hope is alive.
And Jesus is still saving.
